properties.name: Romulus and Remus
properties.summary: Twin sons of Mars and the Vestal Virgin Rhea Silvia, abandoned on the Tiber and raised by a she-wolf. As adults they founded a city, but quarreled over its location. Romulus killed Remus and named the city Rome. The fratricide shadowed Roman history with themes of necessary violence.

properties.name: The Aeneid
properties.summary: After Troy fell, the hero Aeneas journeyed to Italy guided by destiny. He loved and abandoned Queen Dido of Carthage, descended to the underworld, and fought wars in Latium. His descendants would found Rome. Virgil's epic connected Roman power to Trojan heritage and divine mandate.

properties.name: Metamorphoses — Tales of Transformation
properties.summary: Ovid's Metamorphoses weaves 250 transformation myths into a continuous narrative from creation to Julius Caesar's apotheosis. Narcissus becomes a flower, Daphne a laurel tree, Arachne a spider, and Icarus falls from the sky. Each transformation reveals the consequences of hubris, desire, or divine whim.

properties.name: Roman Creation — Ages of Man
properties.summary: The Roman creation myth describes four ages: the Golden Age under Saturn, when the earth yielded crops without labor; the Silver Age; the Bronze Age of warfare; and the Iron Age of suffering. Each age saw moral decline. Saturn's Golden Age became the model for the Saturnalia festival.

properties.name: Proserpina and the Pomegranate
properties.summary: Pluto abducted Proserpina to the underworld. Her mother Ceres caused all plants to die. Jupiter brokered a deal but Proserpina had eaten pomegranate seeds — binding her to six months below. Her annual return brings spring; her departure brings winter. The Eleusinian-style mysteries spread this cult across the Roman Empire.

properties.name: Rape of the Sabine Women
properties.summary: Early Rome had men but no women. Romulus invited the neighboring Sabines to a festival, then his men seized the women. War erupted between Romans and Sabines. The abducted women — now wives and mothers — threw themselves between the armies, demanding peace. The two peoples merged into one nation.
